messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty SEV2 - sustained 5xx spike for inference-api in eu-central-1. AlertID: PD-19834. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (inference-api.redwood.ai).

maya: ack, I'm oncall and looking. Opening bridge and grabbing dashboards.

liam: seeing target group health jump to 45% unhealthy for inference-api-tg in eu-central-1. ELB metrics show surge in 502/504 and 5xx from backend pool. Dashboards: https://grafana.internal/redwood/alerts/PD-19834 :eyes:

sophie: Route53 shows rapid health-check failures for the eu-central record (weighted routing). I also see repeated ENI attach timeouts in instance syslogs on a subset of nodes.

arjun: possible ENI/attachment/backplane issue in az eu-central-1b. Running quick EC2 checks - could be kernel-level netdev flap or ENI quota exhaustion.

net-bot: Runbook excerpt: check ELB target health + ENI attach errors ->
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn $TG_ARN
aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids $(aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn $TG_ARN --query 'TargetHealthDescriptions[].Target.Id' --output text)
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=eu-central-1b
```

maya: running those now. Quick paste: describe-target-health shows 12/26 healthy, most failing with "target: unhealthy, reason: HTTP 502". ec2 describe-network-interfaces returns several ENIs in state 'detaching' and multiple "AttachNetworkInterface: timeout" entries in instance system logs.

liam: suggested mitigation: shift traffic weight off eu-central to eu-west-1 to limit customer impact while we remediate. We can change Route53 weights to 80 (eu-west) / 20 (eu-central) as a temporary measure.

sophie: executing weighted shift now. Using the hosted zone change via console/CLI. CLI command: 
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference-api.redwood.ai.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-central-1","Weight":20,"AliasTarget":{...}}},{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference-api.redwood.ai.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1","Weight":80,"AliasTarget":{...}}}]}'
```

sophie: change submitted (change ID: /change/C0ABC123). Route53 status: PENDING -> IN_PROGRESS. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: System note: DNS change propagation typically ~30-120s; Route53 change created by sophie.

cs-jordan: CS note: drafting customer-facing update. Impact: increased 5xx and degraded latency for eu-central customers. Temporary traffic shifted to eu-west-1 to reduce errors. ETA: under investigation. Posting to status.redwood.ai once we validate.

maya: concurrently scaling up replacement capacity in eu-central — spinning new ASG instances with fresh ENIs and draining unhealthy targets from TG. Starting instance replacement for 3 nodes showing persistent ENI attach failures.

arjun: I'm seeing EBS IO warnings on 2 of the failing instances as well (I/O stalls). We'll detach and reattach new volumes where needed; opening AWS support case in parallel for ENI attach throttling in eu-central-1b.

liam: metrics update: after Route53 weight change, 5xx rate in prod decreased ~70% globally and latency for most requests improved. eu-central still has a small residual error rate from customers that resolve to cached IPs — should decline as TTLs expire.

sophie: replaced 3 instances and replaced one problematic EBS volume; ELB target health now 20/26 healthy. Continuing to monitor.

net-bot: Reminder checklist for handoff: record exact Route53 change ID, TG ARN(s), instance IDs replaced, AWS case number (if opened), and any console screenshots.

maya: handing incident to night oncall (sophie) at 02:00 UTC. Summary for handoff: severity SEV2, impact = intermittent 5xx and higher latency for eu-central, mitigation = Route53 weight shift to eu-west (80/20), replaced 3 instances + 1 EBS volume, ongoing AWS case for ENI attach errors in eu-central-1b. Bridge: https://zoom.internal/redwood/inc-19834. Postmortem owner: liam.

cs-jordan: customer status page update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/19834. Customers notified via email and in-app banner.

liam: follow-ups/tasks assigned: (1) confirm AWS case resolution and share root cause, (2) check ENI quotas and backplane metrics with cloud provider, (3) evaluate improving fallback routing for critical endpoints (Global Accelerator or multi-region active-active).

maya: thanks all — great coordination. Sophie, you own active monitoring overnight, liam owns the postmortem. I'll close bridge once AWS provides an update or tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
